title: Windowed adaptive backlog arbitration to reduce continuous-batcher starvation
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: continuous-batcher tail latency incidents in multi-tenant workloads indicated intermittent starvation of low-throughput routes when high-concurrency KV-heavy requests arrived in bursts. This PR introduces a windowed adaptive backlog arbitration layer that observes short-term queue horizons and dynamically relaxes slot reservation decay per tenant/model to prevent starvation while preserving global throughput and batching efficiency. Design: 1) backlog window sampler: track per-route backlog distribution over a sliding 250ms window (configurable) and compute a backlog score that combines queue length, mean wait, and recent preemption events; 2) adaptive arbitration policy: translate backlog score into a temporary soft-reservation multiplier with exponential decay tuned to workload shape to avoid long-lived priority inversion; 3) humane soft-timeout: replace hard preempt timeouts with jittered, gradually escalating soft timeouts to give KV-heavy requests a chance to finish in degraded kernel paths; 4) KV-cache hinting: add a small hinting hook so the scheduler can mark certain requests for proactive KV prefetch based on backlog trend; 5) observability: new metrics (backlog_score, soft_reservation_factor, humane_timeout_ms) and a console dashboard tile to visualize arbitration activity. Backwards compatibility: all knobs are feature-gated under runtime.flags.windowed_arbitration, default-on in canary clusters only until validated. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on an 8xA100 cluster with realistic mixed workloads (chat embeddings + backend reranking) show 95th token latency reduced by ~18% on samples that previously suffered starvation, median unchanged, end-to-end throughput stable (+1%). Cost per token for the workload showed a 2% improvement due to fewer hedged re-requests. Implementation notes: conservative defaults chosen to avoid excessive batching churn; ability to pin per-tenant policies via config file; unit and bench coverage added. Rollout: staged canary -> region rollout with telemetry checks and automated rollback on spike of hedging or token spillover. See release_notes and docs for tuning guidance.

review_comments: Diego: Can you justify the 250ms window choice? It may be too short for some reranking workloads. Author: perf sweep showed 200-500ms works; 250ms is conservative and configurable via runtime.flags.windowed_arbitration.window_ms.
Lena: Concern about interaction with kv-prefetch causing extra memory pressure. Author: hinting is advisory only and gated; prefetch budget uses same cache admission heuristics to avoid noise.
Marcus: Tests look good but add a flaky guard for bench harness on CI. Author: added retry logic and a bounding cfg so CI bench runs are stable.
